translations.text: These are the words Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, and Lebanon, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.
It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb to Mount Seir and on to Kadesh-barnea.
In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses told the Israelites everything the Lord had commanded him concerning them.
This was after he had killed Sihon, king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this law, saying:
“The LORD our God said to us at Horeb, ‘You have stayed at this mountain long enough.

Turn and set out. Enter the hill country of the Amorites and all its surrounding regions: the Arabah, the hill country, the lowlands, the south, and the seacoast—the land of the Canaanites and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the Euphrates.
See, I have placed the land before you. Go in and take possession of the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give to them and their descendants after them.
And I said to you at that time, “I cannot bear the burden of you by myself.”
The LORD your God has multiplied you, and today you are as numerous as the stars in the sky.
May the Lord, the God of your ancestors, make you a thousand times as numerous as you are and bless you as he promised you.
How, then, can I bear your weight, your burdens, and your disputes by myself?
Choose for yourselves men who are wise, discerning, and known to your tribes, and I will appoint them as your leaders.
You answered me, ‘What you have proposed to do is good.’
I took the heads of your tribes, wise and well-known men, and made them leaders over you: leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, leaders of tens, and scribes for your tribes.
At that time I instructed your judges, saying to them, “Hear the disputes between your fellow Israelites and judge fairly between a man and his fellow Israelite or the foreigner living among them.”

Do not show favoritism in judgment. Hear the small and the great alike. Do not be afraid of anyone, because judgment belongs to God. Bring any case that is too difficult for you to me, and let me hear it.
At that time I instructed you about everything you were to do.

We set out from Horeb and traveled through all that great and terrifying wilderness that you saw, in the land of the hill country of the Amorites, as the Lord our God had commanded us. We came as far as Kadesh-barnea.
I said to you, ‘You have reached the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.
See, the Lord your God has placed the land before you. Go up and take possession of the land, as the Lord, the God of your ancestors, told you. Do not be afraid or terrified.
Then all of you approached me and said, “Let us send men ahead of us to explore the land for us and bring us back a report, showing us the route we should take and the towns we should enter.”
The proposal seemed good to me, so I took twelve men from among you, one man from each tribe.
They turned and went up into the hill country. They went up as far as the Valley of Eshcol and explored the land.
They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it to us. They brought us back a report and told us, “The land that the Lord our God is giving us is good.”
But you were unwilling to go up and rebelled against the command spoken by the LORD our God.
You grumbled from your tents and said, “Because the Lord hates us, he brought us out of the land of Egypt to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us.”

Where are we going up to? Our fellow Israelites have discouraged us, telling us, “The people are larger, taller, and stronger than we are, and the towns are large and fortified up to the sky. We even saw descendants of giants there.”
And I told you, “Do not be afraid or terrified of them.”
The Lord your God goes ahead of you, and he will fight for you, just as he did everything for you in Egypt before your very eyes.
And in the wilderness you saw how the Lord your God nourished you, as a man nourishes his son, throughout all the land you traveled through until you came to this place.
Yet in this matter you do not trust the Lord your God,
He goes ahead of you on the road to prepare a place for you to camp. By fire at night he showed you the road you should take, and by a cloud during the day.
The Lord heard what you said, became angry, and swore an oath, saying,
Not one of these men, this evil generation, will see the good land that I swore to give to your ancestors.
Only Caleb son of Jephunneh will see it. To him and his children I will give the land he walked through, because he followed the Lord wholeheartedly.
The Lord was angry with me too because of you, and he told me, “You too will not enter there.
But Joshua son of Nun, who stands before you, will enter there. Strengthen him, because he will give Israel possession of it.
Your households, which you said would become plunder, and your children, who today do not know good from evil—they will enter there. I will give it to them, and they will take possession of it.
But you must turn back and set out into the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea.”

You answered me, “We have sinned before the Lord our God. We will go up and fight, as the Lord our God commanded us.” Each of you armed himself with his weapons of war, and you were eager to go up into the hill country.
The Lord said to me, “Tell them: Do not go up and do not fight, because I am not among you, so that you will not be defeated before your enemies.”
I told you, but you did not listen. You rebelled against the command of the Lord, acted arrogantly, and went up into the hill country.
The Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you. They chased you like bees stirred up by smoke and drove you from Seir as far as Hormah.
You sat down and wept before the Lord, but the Lord did not listen to your voice or pay attention to you.
You stayed in Rekem for many days, as long as the days you stayed there.
We turned and set out for the wilderness along the road to the Red Sea, as the Lord had told me. We traveled around Mount Seir for many days.
The Lord said to me,
“You have been going around this mountain long enough. Turn north.
Give the people this command: You are about to pass through the territory of your relatives, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, so be very careful.
Do not provoke them, because I will not give you any of their land as an inheritance, not even enough for the sole of a foot to tread on. For I have given Mount Seir to Esau as an inheritance.
Buy grain from them with silver and eat it. Buy water from them with silver as well, and drink it.’”

For the Lord your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has watched over your journey through this wilderness these forty years. The Lord your God has been with you, and you have lacked nothing.
We passed by our relatives, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, leaving the road of the Arabah, Elath, and Ezion-geber. Then we turned and traveled along the road to the wilderness of Moab.

The Lord said to me: Do not harass the Moabites or provoke them to battle, because I will not give you any of their land as an inheritance. For I have given it to the descendants of Lot as an inheritance.
The Emim lived there formerly, a great and numerous people, as tall as giants.
They are giants, and they too are reckoned as giants. The Moabites call them Emim.

The Horites formerly lived in Seir, but the descendants of Esau dispossessed them, destroyed them from before them, and settled in their land, just as Israel did to the land of its inheritance, which the Lord gave them.
“Now get up and cross the Zered Valley.” So we crossed the Zered Valley.

The time we spent traveling from Rekem of the Valley until we crossed the Zered Valley was thirty-eight years, until the entire generation of fighting men had perished from the camp, as the Lord had sworn to them.
The Lord’s hand was also against them, to destroy them from the camp until they were all gone.
When all the fighting men among the people had finished dying,
the Lord spoke to me and said,
“Today you are crossing into the territory of Moab and Ar.

When you approach the Ammonites, do not harass them or provoke them, because I will not give you any of the Ammonites’ land as an inheritance. For I have given it to the descendants of Lot as an inheritance.
It too is reckoned as a land of giants. Giants formerly lived there, and the Ammonites call them Zamzummim.
They were a great and numerous people, tall like giants. The Lord destroyed them before the Ammonites, who dispossessed them and settled in their land.
This is what the descendants of Esau who live in Seir did: they destroyed the Horites from before them, dispossessed them, and settled in their land, where they remain to this day.
As for the Avvim who lived in Hazerim as far as Gaza, the Cappadocians who came out of Cappadocia destroyed them and settled in their land.
Now get up, set out, and cross the Arnon Valley. See, I have handed over to you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to destroy him, and engage him in battle.
Today I will begin to put the dread and fear of you upon the peoples under heaven. They will hear reports of you, tremble, and be afraid of you.
I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying to him:
“Let us pass through your land. We will stay strictly on the road and will not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Sell us grain for money so that we may eat, and sell us water for money so that we may drink. We will only pass through on foot,
just as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in [?] did for us, until we cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord our God is giving us.

But Sihon king of Heshbon was unwilling to let us pass through his territory, because the Lord your God had made his spirit stubborn and hardened his heart, so that he might hand him over to you, as he has now done.
The Lord said to me: See, I have begun to hand Sihon and his land over to you. Begin to destroy him and take possession of his land.
Sihon came out to meet us, he and all his people, for battle at Jahaz.
The Lord our God handed him over to us, and we struck him down, along with his sons and all his people.
We captured all his towns at that time and completely destroyed all the towns, along with the women and households. We left none of them alive.
We took only the livestock for ourselves as plunder, along with the spoil from the towns we had captured.
From Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley, including the town in the valley, as far as Gilead, there was no town too strong for us. The Lord our God handed them all over to us.
Only you did not approach the land of the Ammonites: all the territory along the Jabbok Valley, the towns of the hill country, and everything concerning which the Lord our God had commanded us.
We turned and went up along the road to Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to fight at Edrei.
The Lord said to me, “Do not be afraid of him, for I have handed him over to you, along with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
The Lord our God also handed over to us Og king of Bashan and all his people. We destroyed him and left him no survivor.
We captured all his towns at that time. We left no town that we did not take from them: sixty towns, the whole region of Argob, the royal domain of Og in Bashan.
All these towns had strong walls, high gates, and bars, besides the very many unwalled towns.
We destroyed them, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, whose towns we had completely destroyed, along with the women and households.
We took all the livestock and the spoil of the towns for ourselves as plunder.
At that time we took the land from the two kings of the Amorites who were across the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley as far as Mount Hermon.
The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.
And all the towns of the plain, all Gilead, and all Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei—all the towns of Og’s kingdom in Bashan.

For Og king of Bashan alone remained of the remnant of the giants. His bed was an iron bed. It is there in Rabbah of the Ammonites: nine cubits long and four cubits wide, measured by the cubit of the giants.
We took possession of this land at that time. I gave Reuben and Gad the land from Aroer, on the bank of the Arnon Valley, and half the hill country of Gilead with its towns.
I gave the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, Og’s royal domain, to the half-tribe of Manasseh. The whole region of Argob and all Bashan are called the land of the giants.
Jair son of Manasseh took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of Geshur and Maacah. He named them after himself: Bashan and the villages of Jair, as they are called to this day.
I gave Gilead to Machir.
To Reuben and Gad I gave the land from Gilead as far as the Arnon Valley, including the middle of the valley as its boundary, and as far as the Jabbok, the valley forming the border of the Ammonites.
And the Arabah and the Jordan, with the boundary extending from Chinnereth as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, below Ashdod and Pisgah, in the highlands to the east.
At that time I commanded you, saying, “The Lord your God is giving you this land to possess. Cross over armed ahead of your fellow Israelites, all of you mighty warriors.
Leave behind only your wives, your households, and your livestock, for I know that you have many possessions. Let them stay in the towns I have given you,

until the Lord gives your fellow Israelites rest as he has given you, and they too possess the land that the Lord your God is giving you across the Jordan. Then each of you may return to the property I have given you.”
At that time I commanded Joshua, saying, “Your eyes have seen everything the Lord your God has done to these two kings. The Lord will do the same to all the kingdoms into which you are crossing.”
Do not be afraid of them, because the Lord your God is the one who fights for you.
At that time I pleaded before the Lord and said:

“I beg you, Lord God, you have begun to show your servant your greatness, your mighty hand, and your uplifted arm. For what god is there in heaven or on earth who can do deeds like yours and mighty acts like yours?”
Let me now cross over and see the good land beyond the Jordan, this good hill country and Lebanon.”
But the Lord was angry with me because of you and would not listen to me. The Lord said to me, “Enough! Do not speak to me again about this matter.
Go up to the top of the height. Look up toward the east and west, the north and south, and see it with your own eyes, for you will not cross this Jordan.
Commission Joshua, encourage him, and strengthen him, because he will cross over ahead of this people, and he will give them possession of the land you will see.”
And we stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor.
Now, Israel, listen to the laws and judgments that I am teaching you today to carry out, so that you may live and enter and possess the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.
Do not add to the command I am giving you, and do not take away from it. Instead, keep the command of the Lord your God that I am giving you.
Your own eyes saw everything the Lord did to Baal-peor, for the Lord your God destroyed from among you everyone who followed Baal-peor.
But you who held fast to the LORD your God are all still alive today.
See, I have taught you laws and judgments, just as the Lord my God commanded me, so that you may carry them out in the land you are entering to possess.
Keep them and carry them out, for this is your wisdom and understanding in the eyes of the nations. They will hear all these laws and say, “This great nation is indeed wise and discerning.”
For what great nation has its god near it, as the LORD our God is whenever we call on him?
And what great nation has laws and judgments as just as this entire law that I am setting before you today?

Only be very careful and guard yourselves, so that you do not forget all the things your eyes have seen, and they do not depart from your hearts all the days of your lives. Make them known to your children and your grandchildren.

The day you stood before the Lord your God at Horeb, the Lord said to me, “Gather the people before me, and I will let them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me all the days they live on earth and may teach their children.”
You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain. The mountain was blazing with fire up to the heart of the heavens, with darkness, cloud, and thick gloom.
The Lord spoke with you on the mountain from within the fire. You heard the sound of speech, but you saw no form—only a voice.
He made his covenant known to you and commanded you to carry out the Ten Commandments. He wrote them on two stone tablets.
At that time the Lord commanded me to teach you laws and judgments, so that you would carry them out in the land you are crossing over to possess.
Be very careful to guard yourselves, for you saw no form on the day the Lord spoke with you at Horeb from within the fire.
Do not become corrupt and make yourselves carved images and likenesses of any kind, in the form of a male or a female.
a likeness of any animal on the earth, a likeness of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
a likeness of anything that crawls on the ground, or a likeness of any fish in the sea beneath the earth.

Do not raise your eyes to heaven and see the sun, the moon, the stars, and all the host of heaven, and be led astray to bow down to them and serve them. The Lord your God has allotted them to all the peoples under heaven...
But the Lord brought you near and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be his people and his inheritance, as you are today.
The Lord was angry with me because of your words, and he swore that I would not cross this Jordan or enter the good land that the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance.
For I will die in this land and will not cross this Jordan. But you will cross over and take possession of this good land.
Be careful not to forget the covenant of the Lord your God that he made with you, and not to make yourselves carved images and likenesses of anything concerning which the Lord your God commanded you.
For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

When you have children or grandchildren, and they grow old in the land, and you become corrupt and make carved images and likenesses of anything, and do what is evil before the Lord your God and provoke him to anger,

I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that you will certainly perish quickly from the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess. You will not live long in it, but will be utterly destroyed.
The Lord will scatter you among the nations, and you will be left few in number among the nations to which the Lord your God will scatter you.
There you will serve other gods, the work of human hands, made of wood and stone, which neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell.
There you will seek the Lord your God and find him when you search for him with all your heart and all your soul.
When you are in distress and all these things have come upon you in the latter days, you will turn back to the Lord your God and obey his voice.
For the Lord your God is a merciful God. He will not destroy you or abandon you, and he will not forget the covenant he swore to your ancestors.

But ask about the former days that came before you, from the day God created humankind on the earth, from one end of heaven to the other: has anything as great as this ever happened, or has anything like it ever been heard?
Has any other people heard the voice of God speaking from within the fire, as you have heard, and lived?

Or has God been put to the test to go and take for himself a people from among another people, through trials, signs, wonders, wars, a mighty hand, an uplifted arm, and great sights—all that the LORD your God did to the Egyptians before your eyes?
You have seen and have come to know that the Lord is God, and there is no other besides him.
From heaven he made you hear his voice to instruct you, and on earth he showed you his great fire. He made you hear his words from within the fire.
Because he loved your ancestors, he chose their descendants after them and brought you out of Egypt by his own presence and with great power,
to destroy before you nations greater and stronger than you, to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance, as it is today.
Know today and take it to heart that the LORD is God in heaven above and on the earth below. There is no other besides him.

Keep his laws and his commandments, which I command you today, so that it may go well with you and your children after you, and you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you for all time.
Then Moses set apart three towns beyond the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
So that someone who kills his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him previously, may flee there. He may flee to one of these towns and live.
One of them was Bezer in the wilderness, in the land of the plain belonging to Reuben; another was Ramoth-gilead, belonging to Gad; and Golan in Bashan, belonging to Manasseh.
This is the law that Moses set before the Israelites.
These are the testimonies, laws, and judgments that Moses spoke to the Israelites when they came out of Egypt,
beyond the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon. Moses and the Israelites killed him when they came out of Egypt.
They took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan—the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise—
From Aroer [?], on the bank of the Arnon Valley, as far as Mount Sirion, which is Hermon.
and all the Arabah east of the Jordan, as far as the Sea of the Arabah below Ashdod and Pisgah.
Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, “Listen, Israel, to the laws and judgments that I am speaking before you today, so that you may learn them, keep them, and carry them out.
The Lord our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
It was not with our ancestors that the LORD made this covenant, but with us, all of us who are here alive today.
The Lord spoke with you face to face on the mountain, from within the fire.
At that time I stood between the LORD and you to make known to you the words of the LORD your God, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
You must have no other god besides me.
Do not make for yourself any image or any likeness of anything in heaven above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath the earth.
Do not bow down to them or worship them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, punishing the children for the sins of their fathers to the third and fourth generations of those who hate me.
And I show kindness to thousands of generations, to those who love me and keep my commandments.
Do not swear falsely by the name of the LORD your God, for the LORD will not acquit anyone who swears falsely by his name.
Observe the Sabbath day and keep it holy, as the Lord your God commanded you.
Work for six days and do all your work.

The seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. Do not do any work on it—you, your son, your daughter, your male slave, your female slave, your ox, your donkey, any of your livestock, or the foreign resident living in your towns—so that your male and female slaves may rest as you do.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out of there with a mighty hand and an uplifted arm. That is why the LORD your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God commanded you, so that you may live long and it may go well with you in the good land that the LORD your God is giving you.
Do not murder.
Do not commit adultery.
Do not steal.
Do not give false testimony against your neighbor.
Do not covet your neighbor’s wife. Do not covet your neighbor’s house, his field, his vineyard, his male slave, his female slave, his ox, his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.

The LORD spoke these words to your whole assembly on the mountain, from within the fire, in the cloud and thick darkness, with a mighty voice without limit. He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
When you heard the voice from within the darkness, while the mountain was blazing with fire, you came to me—all your tribal leaders and your elders.

And you said, “Look, the LORD our God has shown us his glory and greatness, and we have heard his voice from within the fire. Today we have seen that God can speak with a human being and that person can live.
Now why should we die and this great fire consume us? If we go on hearing the voice of the LORD our God, we will die.
For what mortal like us has heard the voice of the living God speaking from within the fire and remained alive?
You go near and hear everything that the LORD our God says to you. Then tell us everything that the LORD our God says to you, and we will listen and do it.”
The LORD heard your words as you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, “I have heard the voice of this people and the words they have spoken to you. Everything they have said is good.
If only they would always have this heart, to fear me and keep all my commandments, so that it might go well with them and their children forever!
Go and tell them, ‘Return to your tents.’
But you, stand here before me, and I will tell you all my commandments, laws, and judgments, which you are to teach them, so that they may carry them out in the land I am giving them to possess.”
Be careful to do as the Lord your God has commanded you. Do not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Walk in the whole way that the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live, that it may go well with you, and that you may live long in the land you will possess.
These are the commandments, laws, and judgments that the LORD your God commanded me to teach you, so that you may carry them out in the land you are entering to possess.
You are to fear the LORD your God and keep all his commandments, laws, and judgments that I command you—you, your son, and your grandson—all the days of your life, so that you may live long.

Listen, Israel, and be careful to carry them out, so that it may go well with you and you may become very numerous, just as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, promised you that he would give you a land flowing with milk and honey.
Listen, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one.
Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your possessions.
Let these words that I command you today be on your heart.
Repeat them to your children, and speak about them when you sit in your house, when you walk along the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
Bind them as a sign on your hand, and let them be a mark between your eyes.
Write them on the thresholds of your houses and on your gates.
When the LORD your God brings you into the land that he swore to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give them, giving you large and good towns that you did not build,
and houses full of every good thing that you did not fill, dug wells that you did not dig, and vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant, and you eat and are satisfied,
be careful not to forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
Fear the Lord your God, serve him, and swear by his name.
Do not follow other gods, the gods of the peoples around you.
for the LORD your God among you is a jealous God, lest the anger of the LORD your God burn against you and he destroy you from the face of the earth.
Do not put the Lord your God to the test, as you tested him in the trials.
But keep the commandments of the Lord your God, his testimonies, and his laws that he commanded you.
Do what is good and right before the LORD your God, so that it may go well with you and you may enter and possess the good land that the LORD swore to your ancestors.
and he will crush all your enemies before you, just as the Lord said.
When your son asks you in the future, saying, “What is the meaning of the testimony, the laws, and the judgments that the LORD our God commanded you?”
tell your son, “We were Pharaoh’s slaves in Egypt, and the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
Before our eyes, the LORD performed great signs and wonders and brought calamities upon Egypt, upon Pharaoh, and upon his entire army.
The Lord brought us out of there to bring us in and give us the land that he swore to our ancestors.
The LORD commanded us to carry out all these laws and to fear the LORD our God, so that it might always go well with us and he might keep us alive, as we are today.
It will be righteousness for us when we are careful to carry out this entire commandment before the LORD our God, as he commanded us.”

When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess, and destroys many nations before you—the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, seven nations more numerous and stronger than you—
and the LORD your God delivers them over to you, you must strike them down and utterly destroy them. Make no covenant with them and show them no mercy.
Do not intermarry with them. Do not give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters for your sons.
Otherwise they will turn your children away from me to serve other gods, and the LORD’s anger will burn against you, and he will quickly destroy you.
Instead, this is what you must do to them: tear down their altars, break their sacred pillars, cut down their metal idols, and burn their carved images in the fire.
For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you to be his beloved people out of all the peoples on the face of the earth.
It was not because you were more numerous than all the other peoples that the LORD set his affection on you and chose you, for you are the fewest of all the peoples.

Rather, because the LORD loves you and would keep the oaths he swore to your ancestors, the LORD brought you out with his mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
Know that the LORD your God is God, the faithful God, who keeps his covenant and shows kindness to those who love him and keep his commandments, for a thousand generations.
He repays those who hate him during their lifetime; he repays them by destroying them. He does not wait to repay those who hate him, but repays them during their lifetime.
Keep the commandments, laws, and judgments that I command you today, and carry them out.
If you listen to these judgments, keep them, and carry them out, the LORD your God will keep with you the covenant and the kindness that he swore to your ancestors.

He will love you, bless you, and increase your numbers. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the produce of your land, your grain, your wine, your oil, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep, in the land he swore to your ancestors to give you.
You will be blessed above all peoples. No man or woman among you will be barren, nor will any of your livestock.
The LORD will take every sickness away from you. He will not bring upon you any of the terrible plagues of the Egyptians that you know, but will bring them upon all who hate you.
You shall devour all the peoples whom the LORD your God gives you. Your eye shall have no pity on them, and you shall not worship their gods, for they are snares to you.
If you say in your heart, “These peoples are more numerous than I am. How can I destroy them?”
Do not be afraid of them. Instead, remember everything that the Lord your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:
The great trials that your eyes saw, the signs and wonders, the mighty hand and the uplifted arm—and the LORD your God brought you out. The LORD your God will do the same to all the peoples you fear.
The LORD your God will also send hornets against them until they perish, including those who remain and those who hide from you.
Do not be afraid of them, because the Lord your God is among you, a great and fearsome God.
The LORD your God will destroy these peoples before you little by little. You cannot destroy them quickly, or the wild animals would become too numerous for you.
The LORD your God will hand them over to you, and you shall strike them with a great blow until you destroy them.
He will hand their kings over to you, and you shall wipe out their name from under heaven. No one will stand against you until you have destroyed them.

You shall burn the carved images of their gods in the fire. Do not covet the silver and gold on them and take it for yourself, lest you become defiled by it, for it is detestable to the LORD your God.
Do not bring a detestable thing into your house, lest you become devoted to destruction like it. Instead, utterly despise it and regard it as utterly unclean, for it is devoted to destruction.
Keep all the commandments that I command you today, and carry them out, so that you may live, increase in number, and enter and take possession of the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors.

Remember the whole way that the LORD your God has led you through the wilderness these forty years, to humble you and test you, and to know what was in your hearts, whether you would keep his commandments or not.

He humbled you, made you hungry, and fed you manna, which neither you nor your ancestors had known, to show you that a human being does not live by bread alone, but lives by everything that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
Your clothes did not wear out on you, and your feet did not go bare these forty years.
Know in your heart that just as a man disciplines his son, so the Lord your God disciplines you.
Keep the commandments of the Lord your God, walk in his ways, and fear him.
For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of streams of water, springs, and deep waters flowing out in the valleys and mountains.
A land of wheat and barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates; a land of olives, oil, and honey.
A land where you will not eat bread in poverty, and where you will lack nothing; a land whose stones are iron and from whose mountains you will quarry copper.
You will eat and be satisfied, and you will bless the Lord your God for the good land he has given you.
Be careful not to forget the LORD your God. Instead, keep his commandments, his judgments, and his laws, which I command you today.
Otherwise, when you eat and are satisfied, and build fine houses and live in them,
and your flocks and cattle multiply, and your silver and gold increase, and everything you have increases,
your heart may become proud, and you may forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
He led you through the great and terrifying wilderness, a place of venomous snakes and scorpions, a thirsty region where there was no water. He brought water out of flint rock for you.
And he fed you manna in the wilderness, which your ancestors had not known, to humble you and test you and to do you good in the end.
And you may say in your heart, “By my own power and the strength of my hands I have acquired this wealth.”
Remember the Lord your God, for it is he who gives you the strength to acquire wealth, and who establishes his covenant that he swore to your ancestors, as it is today.
If you forget the Lord your God and follow other gods, serving them and bowing down to them, I testify against you today that you will surely perish.
Like the nations that the Lord destroyed before you, so you will perish if you do not obey the voice of the Lord your God.
Listen, Israel! Today you are crossing the Jordan to go and destroy nations greater and stronger than you, and cities that are large and strong, with walls reaching up to heaven.
They are a great and tall people, descendants of giants, whom you know and about whom you have heard that no one can stand against the giants.

Know today that the Lord your God is the one crossing ahead of you. He is a consuming fire. He will destroy them and crush them before you. You will lay them waste and destroy them quickly, as the Lord has told you.

When the Lord your God has crushed them before you, do not say in your heart, 'Because of my righteousness the Lord has brought me in to possess this land.' For it is because of the sins of these nations that the Lord is destroying them before you.

It is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you are entering to possess their land. Rather, it is because of the sins of these nations that the Lord your God is destroying them before you, and to fulfill the promise that he swore to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Know that it is not because of your righteousness that the Lord your God is giving you this good land to possess, for you are a stubborn people.
Remember, and do not forget, how you angered the Lord your God in the wilderness. From the day you left Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebellious before the Lord.
At Horeb you provoked the Lord to anger, and the Lord was angry enough with you to destroy you.

When I went up the mountain and received the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant that the Lord made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.
The Lord gave me two stone tablets inscribed by the finger of God. On them were all the words that the Lord had spoken to you on the mountain from within the fire on the day of the assembly.
After forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

The Lord said to me, 'Get up and go down from here quickly, because your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have become corrupt. They have quickly turned aside from the way I commanded them and have made themselves a cast-metal idol.'
The Lord said to me, “I have seen this people, and they are indeed a stubborn people.
Now leave me alone so that I may destroy them and wipe out their name from under heaven. I will make you into a nation stronger and more numerous than they are.
I turned and came down the mountain, and the mountain was blazing with fire. The two tablets of the covenant were in my two hands.
I saw that you had sinned against the Lord your God and had made yourselves a cast-metal calf. You had quickly turned aside from the way the Lord your God had commanded you.
I took hold of the two tablets, threw them from my two hands, and broke them before your eyes.
I prayed before the Lord as before, for forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water because of all the sins you had committed, doing what was evil before the Lord and angering him.
For I was afraid of the wrath and anger with which the Lord was angry with you, intending to destroy you. But the Lord listened to me that time too.
The Lord was also very angry with Aaron, ready to destroy him, and I prayed for Aaron too at that time.

I took the calf you had sinfully made and burned it in the fire. I crushed it and ground it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust, and I threw its dust into the stream that flowed down the mountain.
At Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah, you provoked the Lord to anger.

When the Lord sent you from Kadesh-barnea and said to you, 'Go up and possess the land I have given you,' you rebelled against the command from the Lord's mouth. You did not believe him or obey his voice.
You have been rebellious before the Lord from the day I came to know you.
I prayed before the Lord for forty days and forty nights because the Lord had said he would destroy you.
I prayed before the Lord and said, 'Lord God, do not destroy your people and your inheritance, whom you redeemed by your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.'
But remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not look at the stubbornness of this people, or at their wickedness and their sins.

Otherwise, the inhabitants of the land from which you brought them out will say, “Because the Lord did not have the power to bring them into the land he promised them, and because he hated them, he brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.”
Yet they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out by your great power and your uplifted arm.
At that time the Lord said to me, “Cut two stone tablets for yourself like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain. Make yourself a wooden ark.
I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke. Put them in the ark.”
So I made an ark of boxwood and cut two stone tablets like the first ones. I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hands.
He wrote on the tablets, just as he had written before, the ten commandments that the Lord spoke to you on the mountain from within the fire on the day of the assembly. Then the Lord gave them to me.
I turned and came down from the mountain and put the tablets in the ark I had made. I left them in it, as the Lord had commanded me.
The Israelites set out from Beeroth of the sons of Jaakan for Moserah. Aaron died there and was buried there, and his son Eleazar served as priest after him.
From there they set out for Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah for Jotbathah, a land of streams of water.
At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the Lord’s covenant, to stand before the Lord and serve him, and to bless the Lord’s name, as they do to this day.
For this reason Levi had no share or inheritance with his brothers, for the Lord is his inheritance, as the Lord your God told him.
I stood before the Lord on the mountain, as I had before, for forty days and forty nights. The Lord listened to me that time too, and the Lord was unwilling to destroy you.
The Lord said to me, “Get up, set out, and go ahead of the people, so that they may enter and take possession of the land I swore to their ancestors to give them.”
And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God ask of you except to fear the Lord your God, to walk in his ways, to love him, and to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul,
and to keep the commandments of the Lord your God and his laws, which I command you today, so that it may go well with you?
The heavens and the highest heavens, the earth and everything in it, belong to the LORD your God.
Yet the Lord took delight in your ancestors alone and loved them, and he chose their descendants after them from among all the peoples, as it is today.
Circumcise the foreskin of your hearts, and no longer stiffen your necks.
For the Lord your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and awesome God, who shows no partiality and accepts no bribe.
He provides justice for orphans and widows, and loves the one who turns to him, giving him food and clothing.
Love those who turn to him, because you were foreigners living in the land of Egypt.
Fear the Lord your God, serve him, cling to him, and swear by his name.
For he is your praise, and he is your God, who has done for you these great and fearsome things that your own eyes have seen.
Your ancestors went down to Egypt as seventy people, and now, look, the Lord your God has made you as numerous as the stars in the sky.
Love the Lord your God and always keep his requirements, his laws, his judgments, and his commandments.
Know today that this was not for your children, who have neither known nor seen the discipline of the Lord your God, his greatness, his mighty hand, and his uplifted arm,
and his signs and the deeds he did in Egypt to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his whole land,
and what he did to the Egyptian army, to the horses, the chariots, and their riders: he made the waters of the Red Sea flow over them as they pursued you, and the Lord destroyed them to this day.
And everything he did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place.

And what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, the son of Reuben: the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their children, their tents, and everything they owned that stood on its feet, in the midst of all Israel.
Rather, your own eyes have seen all the great deeds that the Lord has done.
Keep all the commandments that I command you today, so that you may be strong and enter and take possession of the land you are crossing over to possess.
Then you will live long in the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors to give to them and their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt from which you came out, where you sowed your seed and watered it with your feet, like an irrigated garden.
But the land you are crossing over to possess is a land of mountains and valleys, watered by rain from heaven.
It is a land that the Lord your God continually cares for. The eyes of the Lord your God are on it from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
And if you obey the commandments I am giving you today, and love the Lord your God and serve him with all your heart and all your soul,
I will give rain for your land in its season, the early rain and the late rain, and you will gather your grain, your wine, and your oil.
I will give grass in your fields for your livestock, and you will eat and be satisfied.
Be careful that your hearts are not deceived, and that you do not turn aside, serve other gods, and bow down to them.

And the Lord’s anger will burn against you, and he will shut up the heavens so that there is no rain, and the land will not yield its crops. You will quickly perish from the good land that the Lord your God is giving you.
Place these commandments in your heart and soul. Tie them as a sign on your hands, and let them be a mark between your eyes.
Teach them to your children so that they speak about them when you sit in your houses, when you walk along the road, when you lie down, and when you get up.
Write them on the thresholds of your houses and on your gates.
So that your days and your children’s days may be many in the land that the Lord your God swore to your ancestors to give them, as long as the heavens remain above the earth.
And if you keep all these commandments that I am giving you today and carry them out, love the Lord your God, walk in all his ways, and hold fast to him,
The Lord will destroy all these nations before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and stronger than you.
Every place where the sole of your foot treads will be yours. From the wilderness and Lebanon, and from the river to the River Euphrates, and as far as the western sea, will be your territory.
No one will stand against you. The Lord your God will put fear and dread of you throughout all the land on which you tread, as the Lord told you.
See, I am setting blessings and curses before you today:
blessings if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today,
And curses, if you do not obey the commandments of the Lord your God, and if you turn aside from the way I am commanding you today and follow other gods whom you do not know.
When the Lord your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess, pronounce the blessings on Mount Gerizim and the curses on Mount Ebal.
Look, they are across the Jordan, beyond the road toward the setting sun, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal and opposite the place of the oak of Mamre.
For you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess the land that the Lord your God is giving you. You will possess it and live in it.
Keep and carry out all the laws and judgments that I am setting before you today.
These are the laws and judgments that you must observe and carry out in the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors, is giving you to possess, all the days you live on the earth.
Destroy all the places where the nations you are dispossessing worshiped their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills, and beneath every tree that gives shade.
Tear down their altars, break their sacred pillars, burn their cast images in the fire, and break their carved gods. Wipe out their name from that place.
You must not worship the Lord your God in this way.
Instead, seek out the dwelling place of the Lord your God at the place he chooses from among all your tribes to establish his name there, and go there.
Bring there your whole burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, the contributions from your hands, your vows, your offerings, and the firstborn of your cattle and your flocks.
Eat there before the Lord your God, and rejoice in everything you undertake, you and your households, because the Lord your God has blessed you.
You must not do as we are doing here today, each person doing what seems right in his own eyes.
For you have not yet reached the resting place and the inheritance that the Lord your God is giving you.
Cross the Jordan and settle in the land that the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance. He will give you rest from all your enemies around you, and you will live securely.

Bring to the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to dwell everything I command you: your whole burnt offerings, your sacrifices, your tithes, the contributions from your hands, and all the choicest offerings that you vow to the Lord.
Rejoice before the Lord your God, you, your sons and daughters, your male and female slaves, and the Levites in your towns, because they have no inheritance or share with you.
Be careful not to offer your whole burnt offering wherever you please.
But only at the place that the Lord chooses in one of your tribes shall you offer your whole burnt offerings. There you shall do everything I command you.

However, you may slaughter animals and eat meat whenever you desire, according to the blessing that the Lord your God gives you, in any of your towns. Both the unclean and the clean may eat it, as they would gazelle or deer.
Only you must not eat the blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.

You are not permitted to eat in your towns the tithes of your grain, wine, or oil, the firstborn of your cattle or sheep, any of the offerings you have vowed to give, your offerings, or the contributions from your hands.

Instead, you must eat them before the Lord your God, in the place that the Lord your God chooses for himself—you, your son and daughter, your male and female slaves, and the Levite in your towns. You must rejoice before the Lord your God in everything you undertake.
Be careful not to neglect the Levites for as long as you live in the land.
When the Lord your God enlarges your territory, as he promised you, and you say, “I will eat meat,” because you desire to eat meat, you may eat meat whenever you desire.

If the place that the Lord your God chooses to put his name there is far from you, slaughter animals from the cattle and sheep that the Lord your God has given you, as I commanded you, and eat in your towns whenever you desire.
But you must eat it just as gazelle and deer are eaten. The unclean and the clean alike may eat it.
Only be firm in not eating the blood, because the blood is the life. You must not eat the life with the meat.
You must not eat it. Pour it out on the ground like water.
You must not eat it, so that things may go well with you and your children after you, when you do what is right before the Lord your God.
But take the holy offerings you have and your vowed offerings, and come to the place the Lord chooses.
Offer your whole burnt offering, both flesh and blood, on the altar of the Lord your God. The blood of your sacrifices must be poured out on the altar of the Lord your God, but you may eat the meat.
Observe and obey all these commandments that I command you today, so that things may go well with you and your children after you forever, when you do what is good and right before the Lord your God.
When the Lord your God destroys the nations to which you are going, and destroys them from before you, and you dispossess them and live in their land,

be careful not to be led astray after them once the Lord has destroyed them from before you. Do not inquire about their gods, saying, “How did these nations worship their gods? I will do the same as they did.”
You must not do this to the Lord your God, because they did for their gods everything that the Lord rejects and hates. They even burned their sons and daughters in the fire for their gods.
Be careful to carry out every command that I give you. Do not add to it or take away from it.
When a prophet or a dreamer of dreams arises among you and gives you a sign and a wonder,
And the sign or wonder that he told you about comes to pass, and he says to you, “Come, let us follow other gods whom you have not known, and let us worship them.”
Do not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer of dreams, because the Lord your God is testing you to find out whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul.
Follow the Lord your God, fear him, keep his commandments, obey him, worship him, and hold fast to him.

That prophet or that dreamer of dreams must be put to death, because he spoke wickedness before the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery, to lead you astray from the path that the Lord your God commanded you to follow. You must remove the evil from among you.

If your brother, your mother's son, or your son or daughter, or the wife of your covenant, or your friend who is like your own soul, secretly entices you and says to you, “Come, let us go and worship other gods whom neither you nor your ancestors have known,”
gods of the peoples around you, whether near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other,
do not be persuaded by him or listen to him. Do not look on him with pity, show him mercy, or conceal him.
Instead, you must certainly put him to death. Your hand must be the first against him to kill him, and afterward the hands of all the people.
Stone him to death, because he sought to lead you astray from the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.
All the house of Israel will hear and be afraid, and they will no longer do such an evil thing among you.
When you hear in one of your towns that the Lord your God is giving you to live in, and people tell you,
Sinful men have gone out from among you and led the people of their town astray, saying, “Let us go and worship other gods whom you have not known.”
Investigate, examine, and inquire thoroughly whether the report is indeed true and this abomination has been committed among you.
Destroy the inhabitants of that town with the sword. Destroy it and everything in it, and kill its livestock with the sword.
Gather all its plunder into its public square. Burn the town and all its plunder completely with fire before the Lord your God. It shall remain a mound of ruins forever and shall never be rebuilt.

Let nothing devoted to destruction remain in your possession, so that the Lord may turn from his fierce anger, grant you mercy, have compassion on you, love you, and make you numerous, as he swore to your ancestors.
If you obey the voice of the Lord your God, keep his commandments that I am giving you today, and do what is right before the Lord your God.
You are children of the Lord your God. Do not cut yourselves or make bald patches between your eyes in mourning for the dead.
For you are a people holy to the Lord your God. The Lord your God has chosen you to be a people more dearly loved by him than all the peoples on the face of the earth.
Do not eat anything unclean.
These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the lamb, the ewe, and the goat;
the deer, the gazelle, the fallow deer, the ibex, the wild ox, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.
You may eat any animal whose hoof is split and divided in two and that chews the cud.

But among the animals that chew the cud or have hooves divided into two parts, you must not eat these: the camel, the hare, and the rock badger. They chew the cud, but their hooves are not divided. They are unclean for you.
The pig, whose hoof is divided but which does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. Do not eat their meat or touch their carcasses.
These you may eat from everything in the water: eat anything that has fins and scales.
Do not eat anything that does not have fins and scales; it is unclean for you.
You may eat any clean bird.
But these are the ones you must not eat: the eagle;
the kite;
the raven, in its various kinds;
the ostrich and the hawk, in their various kinds;
the owl and the [?].
And the pelican and the roller.
And the stork and the heron according to their kinds, and the wild rooster and the peacock.
All the offspring of these flying creatures are unclean for you. They must not be eaten.
You may eat any clean flying creature.

Do not eat anything unclean. Give it to the resident alien in your towns to eat, or sell it to a foreigner, for you are a people holy to the Lord your God. Do not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
Be sure to set aside a tenth of all the produce of your seed that the field yields year after year.

Eat before the Lord your God, in the place he chooses for his name to dwell, the tithes of your grain, wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and your flocks, so that you may learn to fear the Lord your God all your days.
If the journey is too long for you and you cannot carry it, because the place the Lord your God chooses for his name to dwell is far from you, when the Lord your God has blessed you.
sell it for money, tie up the money in your hand, and go to the place the Lord your God chooses.
Buy with the money whatever you desire: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, or anything you wish for. Eat there before the Lord your God and rejoice, you and your household.
Do not abandon the Levite in your towns, because he has no share or inheritance with you.
At the end of three years, bring out the entire tithe of your produce for that year and leave it in your towns.

Let the Levite, who has no share or inheritance with you, and whoever turns to me, and the orphan and the widow in your towns come and eat their fill. Then the Lord your God will bless you in all the work you do with your hands.
At the end of seven years, grant a release from debts.

This is the rule for canceling debts: every creditor shall cancel the debt his neighbor owes him. He shall not demand payment from his neighbor or his brother, because a cancellation of debts has been proclaimed for the Lord.
You may demand payment from a foreigner, but you must cancel whatever your brother owes you.
So that there may be no poor person among you, for the Lord your God will surely bless you in the land the Lord your God is giving you to inherit.
And if you obey the voice of the Lord your God and carefully carry out this entire commandment that I am giving you today.
The Lord your God will bless you as he promised you. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.
If there is a poor person among you, one of your brothers, in any of your towns in the land the Lord your God is giving you, do not harden your heart or close your hand against your poor brother.
Instead, open your hand to him and lend him whatever he lacks.

Be careful not to harbor a wicked thought in your heart, saying, 'The year of debt cancellation, the sabbatical year, is near,' and then look grudgingly at your poor brother and give him nothing. He may cry out to the Lord against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
Instead, give to him, and do not be resentful when you give to him. Because of this, the Lord your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you put your hand to.
For the poor will never disappear from the land. That is why I command you and tell you to open your hand to your poor brother and to the needy in your land.
When your fellow Hebrew, whether a man or a woman, is sold to you, that person shall serve you for six years. In the seventh year, set that person free to leave you.
When you release him from your service as a free man, do not send him away empty-handed.
Instead, set aside provisions and give them to him from your flocks and your cattle, from your threshing floor and your winepress. Give to him from what the Lord your God has given you.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and that the Lord your God redeemed you. That is why I am giving you this command today.
But if he says to you, 'I will not leave you, because I love you and your household, and I am well off with you.'
Take an awl and pierce his ear against the door, and he will be your slave forever. Do the same to your female slave.
Do not resent setting him free and sending him away from you, because he has served you for six years at twice the wages of a hired worker. The Lord your God will bless you in everything you do.
Consecrate to the Lord your God every firstborn male born among your cattle and sheep. Do not work the firstborn of your cattle or shear the firstborn of your sheep.
Instead, eat it before the Lord your God year after year, you and your household, in the place the Lord chooses.
If it has a defect—if it is lame or blind or has any other blemish—do not offer it to the Lord your God.
Instead, eat it in your towns. The unclean and the clean alike may eat it, as you would a gazelle or a deer.
Only you must not eat the blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.
Observe the month of blossoms and celebrate the Passover to the Lord your God, because in the month of blossoms the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
Sacrifice the Passover to the Lord your God from the sheep and cattle, at the place the Lord your God chooses for his name to dwell there.

Do not eat leavened bread with it. Instead, for seven days eat unleavened bread with it, the bread of affliction, because you came out of Egypt in haste. In this way you will remember the day you came out of Egypt all the days of your life.
No leaven shall be seen anywhere within your territory for seven days. None of the meat you sacrifice on the evening of the first day shall remain overnight until morning.
You are not permitted to slaughter the Passover sacrifice in any of your towns that the Lord your God gives you.
Instead, sacrifice the Passover at the place the Lord your God chooses for his name to dwell, in the evening at sunset, at the time when you came out of Egypt.
Cook it and eat it in the place the Lord your God chooses for himself. Then turn back in the morning and go to your tent.
For six days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be an assembly for the Lord your God. You shall do no work on it.
Count seven weeks for yourself. Begin counting the seven weeks when you first put the sickle to the standing grain.
Celebrate the Festival of Weeks to the Lord your God with the contribution you set aside from your own hands, in proportion to how the Lord your God has blessed you.

Rejoice before the Lord your God—you, your son and daughter, your male and female slaves, the Levite in your towns, and the foreign resident, orphan, and widow among you—at the place the Lord your God chooses for his name to dwell there.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt. Keep and carry out all these laws.
Celebrate the Festival of Shelters for seven days when you gather in the produce from your threshing floor and your winepress.
Rejoice at your festival—you, your son and daughter, your male and female slaves, and the Levite, orphan, widow, and foreign resident in your towns.

For seven days celebrate a festival to the Lord your God at the place the Lord chooses, for the Lord your God will bless you in all your produce and in all the work of your hands, and you will rejoice.

Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord your God at the place he chooses: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Booths. Do not appear before the Lord your God empty-handed.
Instead, each person must bring a gift according to what his hand can give, in proportion to the blessing the Lord your God has given you.
Appoint judges and scribes for your tribes in all your towns that the Lord your God gives you. They shall judge the people with righteous judgments.
Do not pervert justice, show partiality, or accept a bribe, because a bribe blinds the eyes of those who are wise in judgment and twists the words of the innocent.
Instead, judge your neighbor fairly, so that you may live and enter and inherit the land that the Lord your God is giving you.
Do not plant saplings of any kind of tree beside the altar of the Lord your God that you make for yourself.
Do not set up a sacred pillar for yourself, something the Lord your God hates.
Do not sacrifice to the Lord your God an ox or a lamb that has a defect or any blemish, because it is unclean before the Lord your God.
If there is found among you, in one of your towns that the Lord your God gives you, a man or woman who does evil before the Lord your God and violates his covenant,
and goes and serves other gods and bows down to them, or to the sun or the moon or any of the host of heaven, which I have not commanded,
and you are told about it and hear of it, investigate thoroughly. If the report is true and this abomination has been committed in Israel,
bring out that man or woman who has done this evil deed in your towns, whether a man or a woman, and stone them to death.
A person deserving death shall be put to death on the testimony of two witnesses or three witnesses. No one shall be put to death on the testimony of one witness.
The witnesses shall be the first to raise their hands against him to put him to death, and afterward all the people. Destroy the evildoers from among you.

If a legal matter is too difficult for you—between one case of bloodshed and another, between one legal claim and another, or between one leprous lesion and another—a disputed matter in your towns, you must get up and go to the place that the LORD your God will choose for himself.
Go to the priest and the Levite, or to the judge who is serving at that time. Inquire, and they will tell you the ruling.
You must act according to the ruling they give you from that place, as the LORD has said. Be careful to do as they instruct you.
Act according to the law they explain to you and the judgment they give you. Do not turn aside from the ruling they give you, either to the right or to the left.
Anyone who acts arrogantly and refuses to obey the priest who stands there to minister before the LORD your God, or the judge, must be put to death. Remove evildoers from Israel.
All the people will hear and be afraid, and they will no longer act arrogantly.
When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, take possession of it, and settle in it, and you say, “I will appoint a king over myself like all these nations around me,”

you must indeed appoint over yourself a king whom the LORD your God chooses. Appoint a king over yourself from among your own people. You are not permitted to appoint a foreigner over yourself, someone who is not one of your own people.
But he must not acquire many horses for himself, lest he send the people back to Egypt as his horses increase. The LORD has told you, “You must never return by this road again.”
He must not take many wives for himself, lest they turn his heart aside, and he must not accumulate excessive silver and gold for himself.
When he sits on his royal throne, he must write for himself in a book a copy of this law, from the one kept before the priest and the Levite.
It must remain with him, and he must read it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God, observe all the words of this law and these commandments, and carry them out.

Then his heart will not become proud above his own people, and he will not turn aside from the commandments, either to the right or to the left, so that he and his sons may reign for many days among the Israelites.
The priest and the Levite shall have no share or inheritance among the Israelites. Instead, they shall eat the LORD’s offerings and his allotted share.
He shall have no inheritance among his brothers, for the LORD is his inheritance, as he told him.
This shall be the priest’s due from the people, from those who slaughter a sacrifice, whether an ox or a sheep: they must give the priest the shoulder, the jaw, and the stomach.
Give him the first of your grain, your wine, and your oil, and the first wool sheared from your sheep.
For the LORD your God has chosen him from all your tribes to stand and minister in the name of the LORD your God, he and his sons, for all time.
If a Levite, one of your own people from anywhere in Israel, comes from the place where he lives, he may come with all his heart’s desire to the place the LORD chooses.
He shall serve in the name of the LORD his God, like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD.
They shall eat equal portions, apart from the proceeds of selling ancestral property.
When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, do not learn to act as those nations do.
No one among you is to make his son or daughter pass through fire, practice divination, perform magic, interpret omens, or practice sorcery.
Or one who practices magic with spells, or one who consults mediums and spiritists, or consults the dead.
For everyone who does these things is unclean before the LORD your God. Because of these defilements, the LORD your God is destroying them before you.
Be blameless before the LORD your God.
For these nations that you are dispossessing listen to mediums and diviners. But the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so.
The LORD your God will raise up for himself a prophet like me from among you, from your brothers. You must listen to him.
This is what you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, “Let me never again hear the voice of the LORD my God or see this great fire, so that I do not die.”
And the LORD said to me, ‘Everything they have said is good.
I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their own people. I will put my words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.
Anyone who does not listen to my words that he speaks in my name—I myself will call him to account.
But a prophet who presumes to speak a word in my name that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods—that prophet must be put to death.
If you say in your heart, ‘How can I recognize a word that the LORD has not spoken?’
When a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the thing does not happen or come true, that is a word the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it arrogantly. Do not be afraid of him.
When the LORD your God destroys the nations whose land the LORD your God is giving you, and you dispossess them and settle in their towns and houses,
set apart three towns for yourself within your land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
prepare the road and divide into three parts the territory of the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, so that anyone who kills someone may flee there.
This is the provision for a killer who kills his neighbor and may remain alive: when he kills his neighbor unintentionally, without having hated him previously.

If someone goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood, and raises his hand with an ax to cut a tree, and the iron head slips off the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies, that person may flee to one of these towns and live.

Otherwise, the avenger of blood might pursue the killer in the heat of his anger, overtake him because the journey is long, and kill him, although he does not deserve a death sentence, since he had not hated his neighbor previously.
That is why I command you and tell you to set apart three towns for yourselves.
When the Lord your God enlarges your territory, as he swore to your ancestors, and gives you all the land that he swore to your ancestors,
if you keep and carry out all these commandments that I command you today—to love the Lord your God and walk in his ways all your days—then you shall add three more towns to these three.
This is so that innocent blood will not be shed in your land, which the Lord your God is giving you, and bloodguilt will not be charged against you.
But if a man hates his neighbor, lies in wait for him, attacks him and strikes him so that he dies, and then flees to one of these towns,
the elders of his town shall send for him, bring him back from there, and hand him over to the avenger of blood, and they shall put him to death.
Do not pity him, but put him to death. Avenge Israel’s innocent blood, so that things may go well for you.
Do not move the ancient boundary that those before you established in the inheritance you will receive in the land that the Lord your God is giving you to possess.

A single witness shall not testify against a person concerning any offense or any sin, whatever sin he may commit. A matter shall be established by the testimony of two witnesses or by the testimony of three witnesses.
If a false witness comes forward against a man and testifies against him about wrongdoing,
Both men involved in the dispute shall stand before the Lord and before the priest and the judge serving in those days.
The judges shall investigate carefully and determine whether he was seeking to give false testimony against his fellow.
Do to him as he intended to do to his brother. Remove the evil from among you.
Those who remain shall hear and be afraid, and shall never again do such an evil thing among you.
Show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

When you go out to battle against your enemies and see horses, chariots, and an army larger than yours, do not be afraid of them, because the Lord your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt, goes with you.
When you approach the battle, the priest must come forward and speak to the people.
Listen, Israel! Today you are approaching battle against your enemies. Do not lose heart or be afraid. Do not tremble or be terrified before them.
For the Lord your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt, goes with you. He will fight on your behalf against your enemies and save you.
The officials shall say to the people, “Who has built a new house but has not dedicated it? Let him go back home, lest he be killed in battle and another man dedicate it.”
“Who has planted a vineyard but has not pressed wine from it? Let him go back home, lest he be killed in battle and another man press its grapes.”
“Who has become engaged to a woman but has not married her? Let him go back home, lest he be killed in battle and another man marry her.”
The officials shall speak further to the people and say, “Who is afraid and trembling at heart? Let him go back home, lest his fellow soldiers lose heart as he has.”
When the officers have finished speaking to the people, the commanders of the armies must take their places at the head of the people.
When you approach a town to fight against it, offer it peace.
If it answers you peacefully and opens its gates to you, all the people found in it shall become your tribute-paying slaves and serve you.
But if it does not make peace with you and wages war against you, besiege it.
The Lord your God will hand it over to you, and you shall kill all its males with the sword.
But take the women, the dependents, the livestock, everything in the town, and all its plunder as spoil for yourself. Eat from the plunder of your enemies that the Lord your God gives you.
Do this to all the towns that are very far from you, which are not towns of these nations.
But in the towns of these nations that the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance, do not leave anything that breathes alive.
Instead, completely destroy them—the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—as the Lord your God commanded you.
So that they do not teach you to practice all the filthy things they used to do for their gods, and you sin before the Lord your God.

When you besiege a town for many days, fighting against it to capture it, do not destroy its trees or wield an iron tool against them, because you eat from them. Yet you cut them down. For a tree in the field is not like a human being, able to flee from you during a siege.
But a tree that you know is not a food-producing tree you may destroy and cut down. Build siegeworks against the town that is at war with you until you capture it.
When someone who has been killed is found lying in a field in the land that the Lord your God is giving you to possess, and it is not known who killed him,
your elders and judges shall go out and measure the distances to the towns surrounding the dead man.
The elders of the town nearest the dead person must take a heifer from the herd that has not been worked and has not pulled under a yoke.
The elders of that town must bring the heifer down to an uncultivated valley that has neither been worked nor sown, and slaughter the heifer there in the valley.

The priests, the descendants of Levi, must come forward, because the Lord your God has chosen them to serve him and to bless in the Lord’s name. Every dispute and every case of injury must be settled according to their pronouncement.
All the elders of that town who are nearest the dead person must wash their hands over the heifer slaughtered in the valley.
They shall declare, “Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it.
“Forgive your people Israel, whom you redeemed, Lord, and do not charge your people Israel with innocent blood.” And they will be forgiven for the bloodshed.
You shall investigate the shedding of innocent blood among you and do what is right before the Lord your God.
When you go out to war against your enemies, and the Lord your God delivers them into your hands, and you take captives from among them,
and you see among the captives a beautiful woman whom you desire and take as your wife,
you shall bring her into your house. She shall shave her head and trim her nails.
She must take off the clothes she wore as a captive and stay in your house, mourning her father and mother for a full month. Afterward you may go in to her and marry her, and she will be your wife.
If you do not want her, let her go free. You must not sell her for money or trade in her, because you have humiliated her.
When a man has two wives, one loved and the other hated, and both the loved wife and the hated wife bear him sons, and the firstborn son belongs to the hated wife,
On the day he leaves his possessions to his sons, he is not permitted to give the firstborn’s position to the loved wife’s son ahead of the hated wife’s son.
