Rather, the firstborn, the hated wife’s son, must receive a double share of everything he possesses, because he is the first of his offspring, and the birthright belongs to him.
When a man has a rebellious and defiant son who does not obey his father or mother, and they discipline him but he does not listen to them,
His father and mother shall seize him and bring him out to the elders of the town, to the gate of his home town.
They must say to the elders of his town, “This son of ours is rebellious and defiant. He does not obey us. He is a glutton and a drunkard.”
All the men of his town must stone him to death. Remove evil from among you, and all Israel will hear and be afraid.
If a man is sentenced to death for a sin, and he is hung on a tree and put to death,

His corpse must not remain overnight on the tree. Instead, bury him that same day, because anyone who blasphemes God is to be hung on a tree. Do not defile your land, which the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance.
If you see your brother’s ox or sheep straying, do not ignore them. You must bring them back to your brother.
If your brother does not live near you, or you do not know him, bring them into your house. They must stay with you until your brother looks for them; then return them to him.
Do the same with his ox, his donkey, and his clothing. Do the same with anything he has lost that you find. You are not permitted to ignore it.
If you see your enemy’s donkey or ox lying fallen on the road, do not ignore them. You must help him get them up.
A woman must not wear men’s clothing, and a man must not wear women’s clothing, because everyone who does these things is unclean before the Lord your God.

When you come across a bird’s nest along the road, in any tree or on the ground, containing chicks or eggs, with the mother sitting over the chicks or eggs, do not take the mother along with her young.
Instead, you must let the mother fly away, but you may take her young for yourself, so that things may go well for you and you may live a long life.
When you build a new house, make a parapet for your roof, so that no one falls from it and brings bloodguilt on your house.
Do not sow your field with mixed seed, lest the produce of the seed you sow and the produce of the vineyard become consecrated.
Do not plow with an ox and a donkey together.
Do not wear fabric made of wool and linen mixed together.
Make tassels for yourself on the four corners of the cloak with which you cover yourself.
If a man marries a woman, has intercourse with her, and then hates her,
And he brings accusations against her and gives her a bad name, saying, “I married this woman and slept with her, but I found no evidence of her virginity.”
Then the young woman’s father and mother must take the evidence of her virginity and bring it out to the elders of the town at the gate.
the young woman’s father shall say to the elders, “I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, but he hates her.”

“Now he has brought accusations against her, saying, ‘I found no evidence of your daughter’s virginity.’ But here is the evidence of my daughter’s virginity.” They must spread the cloth before the elders of the town.
The elders of the town shall take that man and discipline him.

They must fine him a hundred pieces of silver and give them to the young woman’s father, because he has given a bad name to a virgin of Israel. She must remain his wife, and he must not be allowed to divorce her as long as he lives.
But if this accusation is true, and no evidence of the young woman’s virginity is found,

They must bring the young woman out to the entrance of her father’s house, and the men of her town must stone her to death, because she has done a shameful thing in Israel by having illicit sex while in her father’s house. You must remove the evil from among you.
When a man is found sleeping with another man’s wife, both of them must be put to death—the man who slept with her and the woman herself. You must remove the evil from Israel.
If a young virgin is engaged to a man, and another man finds her in the town and sleeps with her,

bring both of them out to the gate of that town and stone them to death: the young woman because she did not cry out in the town, and the man because he violated his neighbor’s wife. You must remove the evil from among you.
But if a man finds an engaged young woman in the countryside, seizes her by force, and sleeps with her, only the man who slept with her must be put to death.
You must do nothing to the young woman, because she is not guilty of a sin deserving death. This case is like that of a man who attacks his neighbor and murders him.
For he found her in the countryside, and the engaged young woman cried out, but there was no one to rescue her.
If a man finds a young virgin who is not engaged, seizes her, and sleeps with her, and they are discovered,
the man who slept with her must give the young woman’s father fifty pieces of silver. She must become his wife because he violated her, and he must not be allowed to divorce her as long as he lives.
A man shall not marry his father’s wife or uncover his father’s skirt.
An adulterer shall not enter the assembly of the Lord.
No one born of adultery may enter the assembly of the Lord. Even to the tenth generation, he may not enter the assembly of the Lord.
No Ammonite or Moabite may enter the assembly of the Lord. Even to the tenth generation, they may never enter the assembly of the Lord,
because they did not provide you with bread and water on the way when you came out of Egypt, and because he hired Balaam son of Beor, from Pethor in Aram Naharaim, to curse you.
But the Lord your God was unwilling to listen to Balaam. The Lord your God turned his curses into blessings because the Lord your God loved you.
Do not seek their peace or prosperity all the days of your life, forever.
Do not reject an Edomite, because he is your brother. Do not reject an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.
The children born to them in the third generation may enter the assembly of the Lord.
When you go out in camp against your enemies, guard yourself against everything evil.
If there is a man among you who is unclean because of a nocturnal emission, he must go outside the camp and must not enter the camp.
Toward evening he shall bathe in water, and when the sun has set, he may enter the camp.
You shall have a designated place outside the camp, and you shall go there to relieve yourself.
You must have a digging tool with your equipment. When you squat to relieve yourself, dig with it and cover your excrement.

For the Lord your God walks within your camp to rescue you and deliver your enemies into your hands. Your camp must be holy, so that he does not see anything indecent among you and turn away from you.
Do not hand over to his master a slave who has escaped from his master to you.
Instead, let him live among you wherever he wishes, in whichever of your towns he finds suitable. Do not mistreat him.
There shall be no prostitute among the daughters of Israel, nor shall there be a male prostitute among the sons of Israel.
Do not bring a prostitute’s earnings or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord your God to fulfill any vow, because both are unclean before the Lord your God.
Do not charge your brother interest on money, interest on grain, or interest on anything that bears interest.
You may charge a foreigner interest, but you must not charge your brother interest, so that the Lord your God may bless you in everything you undertake in the land you are entering to possess.
If you make a vow to the Lord your God, do not delay in fulfilling it, because the Lord will certainly require it of you, and you will be guilty of sin.
But if you do not wish to make a vow, you will not be guilty of sin.
Keep and carry out whatever comes from your lips, just as you vowed to the Lord your God—the voluntary offering you promised with your own mouth.
When you enter your neighbor’s vineyard, eat grapes until you are satisfied, but do not put any into your container.
When you enter your neighbor’s standing grain, pluck ears with your hand, but do not swing a sickle over your neighbor’s standing grain.

If a man takes a wife and sleeps with her, but she finds no favor with him because he has found something indecent in her, he shall write her a certificate of divorce, give it to her, and send her away.
She shall leave his house. If she goes and becomes another man’s wife,
And if another man hates her and writes her a certificate of divorce, gives it to her, and sends her away from his house, or if the other man who married her dies,

her first husband, who divorced her, is not permitted to marry her again after she has been defiled, because this is unclean before the Lord. You must not bring sin upon the land that the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance.
When a man takes a new wife, he must not go out with the army or go away on any duty. Instead, he shall stay at home for one year and rejoice with the wife he has married.
Do not take a mill or its upper millstone as security for a loan, for you are putting a person’s life in distress.
If a man from the Israelites is found kidnapping one of his fellow Israelites to trade in that person and sell them, that man must be put to death. Remove the evil from among you.
Watch out for the affliction of leprosy and be very careful. Do as the priests and Levites teach you, just as I commanded them to observe and do.
Remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam on the journey when you came out of Egypt.
If your neighbor owes you a debt of any kind, do not enter his house to take his security.
Instead, stand outside, and the man who owes you shall himself bring the security outside to you.
If he is a poor man, do not sleep in his cloak.
Instead, return his pledge to him when the sun sets, so that he may sleep in his cloak and bless you. This will count as righteousness for you before the Lord your God.
Do not withhold the wages of someone poor and needy, whether one of your brothers or a foreign resident in your towns.

Instead, give him his wages that same day, and do not let the sun set before you pay him, because he is poor and commits himself to your service for his wages. Otherwise, he may cry out against you before the Lord, and you will be guilty of sin.
Fathers must not be put to death because of their children, and children must not be put to death because of their fathers. Each person shall die for their own sins.
Do not pervert justice for a foreign resident or an orphan, and do not take a widow’s cloak as security for a loan.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt and that the Lord your God redeemed you from there. That is why I command you and tell you to do this.

When you reap the harvest of your field and forget a sheaf, do not go back to get it. It shall be for the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow, so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat your olive trees, do not go over them again afterward. What remains shall be for the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow.
When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, do not glean it afterward. What remains shall be for the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.
If there is a dispute between a man and his neighbor, they shall approach the judges, who shall judge them, acquit the innocent, and condemn the guilty.
If the guilty person deserves a beating, the judge shall have him laid down and beaten in his presence, as his offense deserves.
They shall give him forty lashes by count and no more, so that, by adding more lashes beyond this beating, they do not degrade your brother in your eyes.
Do not muzzle an ox while it is threshing.

When brothers live together and one of them dies without a son, the dead man’s wife must not marry a man outside the family. Instead, her husband’s brother shall marry her. She shall become his wife, and he shall fulfill a brother-in-law’s duty toward her.
The firstborn she bears shall be named after his dead brother, so that his name will not be forgotten in Israel.

If the man is unwilling to marry his brother’s wife, his brother’s wife shall go up to the gate, to the elders, and say, “My husband’s brother is unwilling to preserve his brother’s name in Israel. He is unwilling to marry me.”
The elders of his town shall summon him and speak with him. If he stands firm and says, "I will not marry her,"

His brother’s widow shall approach him in the presence of the elders, remove his sandal from his foot, spit in his face, and say, “This is what shall be done to the man who will not build up his brother’s household.”
His household shall be known in Israel as "the household of the man whose sandal was removed."

When a man and his fellow are fighting each other, and the wife of one of them comes forward to rescue her husband from the hands of the man fighting him, and she reaches out her hand and grabs his genitals,
cut off her hand. Show her no pity.
You must not have two different weights in your bag, one large and one small.
You must not have two different measures in your house, one large and one small.
You shall have a full and honest weight, and you shall have an accurate and honest measure, so that your days may be long in the land that the Lord your God is giving you.
For everyone who does these things, everyone who acts unjustly, is unclean before the LORD your God.
Remember everything Amalek did to you along the way when you came out of Egypt:
who met you with the sword and killed all those among you who lagged behind, while you were exhausted and weary. He did not fear the Lord your God.
When the LORD your God gives you rest from all your enemies around you, in the land that the LORD your God gives you as an inheritance, wipe out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget.
When you enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, take possession of it, and settle in it,

Take some of the first of all the produce of the ground that you bring in from the land that the LORD your God gives you, and put it in a basket. Set out and go to the place that the LORD your God chooses for his name to dwell there.
Go to the priest who is serving in those days and say to him, “Today I declare to the LORD your God that I have come into the land that the LORD swore to our ancestors to give us.”
The priest shall take the basket from your hand and set it before the LORD your God.
Then declare before the LORD your God, “My father was led to Aram and went down to Egypt. He lived there for a short time, and there he became a great and mighty nation.”
“The Egyptians mistreated us and oppressed us, and imposed hard labor on us.”
We cried out to the LORD, the God of our ancestors. The LORD heard our voice and saw our humiliation, our hardship, and our oppression.
The LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an uplifted arm, with a great spectacle, with signs and wonders.
“We came to this place, and the LORD gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.”
“And now, look, I have brought the first of the produce of the ground that the LORD has given me.” Place it before the LORD your God and bow down there before the LORD your God.
Rejoice in all the good things that the LORD your God has given you and your household—you, the Levite, and the foreign resident among you.

When you have finished setting aside the whole tithe of your produce in the third year, which is the year of tithes, give it to the Levite, the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow, so that they may eat in your towns and be satisfied.

Say before the LORD your God, “I have removed the sacred portion from the house and given it to the Levite, the foreign resident, the orphan, and the widow, according to all the commandments you gave me. I have not transgressed your commandments or forgotten them.”

I have not eaten any of it while mourning, nor removed any of it while I was unclean, nor set aside any of it for the dead. Instead, I have obeyed the voice of the LORD my God and done as you commanded me.
Look down from your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the land you have given us, as you swore to our ancestors—a land flowing with milk and honey.
Today the LORD your God commands you to carry out these laws and judgments. Keep them and carry them out with all your heart and with all your soul.
Today you have declared to the LORD that he is to be your God, and that you will walk in his ways, keep his laws, judgments, and commandments, and obey his voice.
Today the LORD has declared to you that you are to be his beloved people, as he told you, and that you are to keep all his commandments.
He will set you above all the nations he has made, in praise, renown, and honor, and you will be a people holy to the LORD your God, as he told you.
Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, saying to them, “Keep all the commandments that I am giving you today.”
On the day when you cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD your God gives you, set up large stones for yourself and coat them with plaster.
Write on them all the words of this law when you cross over to enter the land that the LORD your God gives you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, told you.
When you have crossed the Jordan, set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I command you today, and coat them with plaster.
“Build there an altar to the LORD your God, an altar of stones. Do not use an iron tool on them.”
But build the altar of the LORD your God with whole stones, and offer whole burnt offerings on it before the LORD your God.
Sacrifice peace offerings and eat there, and rejoice before the Lord your God.
“Write on the stones all the words of this law, making them very clear.”
Moses, the priests, and the Levites said to all Israel, “Be attentive and listen, Israel! Today you have become the people of the LORD your God.”
“Obey the voice of the LORD your God, and carry out his commandments and his laws that I am giving you today.”
Moses commanded the people that day and said to them:
These are to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people when you have crossed the Jordan: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.
These are to stand on Mount Ebal to pronounce the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.
They shall declare to all the people of Israel in a loud voice:
Cursed is the man who makes carved or cast images, which are unclean before the LORD, the work of a craftsman's hands, and sets them up in secret. All the people shall respond and say, “Amen.”
“Cursed is anyone who insults his father or his mother.” And all the people shall say, “Amen.”
Cursed is anyone who moves his neighbor’s boundary marker. And all the people shall say, “Amen.”
Cursed is anyone who leads a blind person astray on the road. And all the people shall say, “Amen.”
Cursed is anyone who perverts justice for the resident foreigner, the orphan, or the widow. And all the people shall say, “Amen.”
Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his father's wife and uncovers his father's covering. All the people shall say, “Amen.”
Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with any animal. And all the people shall say, “Amen.”
Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with his sister, his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter. And all the people shall say, “Amen.”
Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with his mother-in-law. And all the people shall say, “Amen.”
Cursed is anyone who strikes his neighbor in secret. And all the people shall say, “Amen.”
Cursed is anyone who accepts a bribe to kill an innocent person. And all the people shall say, “Amen.”
Cursed is everyone who does not uphold the words of this law and carry them out. And all the people shall say, “Amen.”
If you obey the voice of the Lord your God and keep and carry out all his commandments that I command you today, the Lord your God will set you above all the nations of the earth.
All these blessings will come upon you and overtake you when you obey the voice of the Lord your God.
Blessed are you in the town, and blessed are you in the field.
Blessed will be the fruit of your womb and the produce of your land, the offspring of your livestock, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
Blessed are your basket and your kneading trough.
Blessed are you when you come in, and blessed are you when you go out.
The Lord will hand over to you, defeated before you, your enemies who rise against you. They will come out against you by one road and flee from you by seven roads.
The Lord will command blessings upon your storehouses and upon everything you put your hand to. He will bless you in the land that the Lord your God is giving you.
The Lord will establish you as a people holy to himself, as he swore to you, if you keep all the commandments of the Lord your God and walk in his ways.
All the peoples of the earth will see that the Lord’s name is proclaimed over you, and they will fear you.
The Lord will make you prosper abundantly in the fruit of your womb, the offspring of your livestock, and the produce of your land, in the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors to give you.

The Lord will open for you his good storehouse, the heavens, and give rain to your land in its season. He will bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.
The Lord will make you the head and not the tail. You will be above and not below, if you obey the commandments of the Lord your God that I command you today, keeping them and carrying them out.
Do not turn aside from any of the commandments that I command you today, either to the right or to the left. Do not follow the gods of the nations and worship them.
But if you do not obey the voice of the Lord your God, and do not keep and carry out all his commandments and laws that I command you today, all these curses will come upon you and overtake you.
Cursed are you in the town, and cursed are you in the field.
Cursed are your basket and your kneading trough.
Cursed will be the offspring of your womb and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle and the flocks of your sheep.
Cursed will you be when you come in, and cursed will you be when you go out.

The Lord will send upon you loss, confusion, and rebuke in everything you put your hand to do, until he destroys you and quickly wipes you out, because of the evil of your deeds, because you have abandoned me.
The Lord will send a plague upon you until he destroys you from the land you are entering to possess.
The Lord will strike you with stupor and a scaly disease, with burning fever and inflammation, with jaundice and the sword, and with a scorching wind. They will pursue you until they destroy you.
The heavens above your head will become bronze, and the earth beneath you will become iron.
The Lord will make the rain of your land into dust. Dirt will descend upon you from heaven until he destroys you.
The Lord will defeat you before your enemies. You will go out against them by one road and flee from them by seven roads. You will become an object of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your corpse will become food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth, and no one will frighten them away.
The Lord will strike you with the boils of the Egyptians, with hemorrhoids, scabies, and an itch from which you cannot be healed.
The Lord will strike you with madness, blindness, and confusion of mind.
You will grope at noon as a blind person gropes in the darkness. You will not succeed in your undertakings. You will be driven by force and oppressed all your days, with no one to rescue you.
You will become engaged to a woman, but another man will marry her. You will build a house, but you will not live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but you will not press wine from it.

Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, but you will not eat any of it. Your donkey will be taken from you by force and will not be returned to you. Your sheep will be handed over to your enemies, with no one to rescue them.
Your sons and daughters will be handed over to another people while your eyes look on. You will grieve over them all day, but your hands will be powerless.
A people you do not know will eat the produce of your land and everything you have labored for. You will be oppressed and afflicted all your days.
You will be driven mad by the sights your eyes see.
The Lord will strike you with terrible boils on your knees and legs, from which you cannot be healed, from the sole of your foot to the crown of your head.
The Lord will lead you and the king you have set over you away to a people whom neither you nor your ancestors have known. There you will worship other gods, made of wood and stone.
You will become an object of horror, a proverb, and a subject of mockery among all the peoples to whom the Lord scatters you.
You will take much seed out to your field, but you will gather little, because the locusts will eat it.
You will plant and cultivate a vineyard, but you will neither drink its wine nor gather its harvest, because worms will eat it.
You will have olive trees throughout your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with oil, because your olives will fall off.
You will have sons and daughters, but they will not remain yours, because they will go into captivity.
Crickets will devour all your trees and the produce of your land.
The foreigner living among you will rise higher and higher above you, while you sink lower and lower.
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.

All these curses will come upon you, overtake you, and pursue you until they destroy you, because you did not obey the voice of the Lord your God and did not keep his commandments and laws that he commanded you.
They will be signs and wonders upon you and your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and gladness of heart when you had an abundance of everything.
You will serve your enemies whom the Lord sends against you, in hunger, thirst, nakedness, and lack of everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until he destroys you.
The Lord will bring against you a nation from far away, from the ends of the earth, like an eagle swooping down—a nation whose language you do not understand.
A fierce-faced nation that shows no respect for the elderly and no mercy to children.
It will eat the offspring of your livestock and the produce of your land until it destroys you. It will leave you no grain, wine, or oil, no herds of cattle or flocks of sheep, until it destroys you.

It will besiege you in all your towns until it brings down the high, strong walls in which you trust throughout your land. It will besiege you in all your towns throughout the land that the Lord your God is giving you.
You will eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and daughters whom the Lord your God has given you. You will eat them during the siege and distress that your enemy brings upon you.
The most delicate and pampered man among you will look grudgingly at his brother, at the wife of his covenant, and at the children he still has left.
He will not give any of them any of the flesh of his children that he is eating, because he will have nothing left during the siege and distress that your enemy brings upon you in all your towns.

The delicate and pampered woman among you, who has never been accustomed to setting the sole of her foot on the ground because of her delicate and pampered life, will look grudgingly at her husband, her son, and her daughter,

over her afterbirth that comes out from between her legs and the child she bears, for she will eat them when she lacks everything, during the siege and distress that your enemy brings upon you in all your towns.
If you do not carefully carry out all the words of this law that are written in this book, and fear this glorious and awe-inspiring name, the Lord your God,
then the Lord will make the plagues upon you and your descendants extraordinary: great and persistent plagues, and severe and lasting illnesses.
He will bring upon you all the plagues of the Egyptians that you fear, and they will cling to you.
The Lord will bring upon you every sickness and every plague not written in this book of the law, until he destroys you.
You will be left few in number, although you were as numerous as the stars in the sky, because you did not obey the voice of the Lord your God.

Just as the Lord delighted in doing you good and making you numerous, so the Lord will delight in destroying you and bringing you to an end. You will be removed from the land you are entering to possess.
The Lord will scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will worship other gods, made of wood and stone, which neither you nor your ancestors have known.
Among those nations you will find no peace, and the sole of your foot will have no resting place. There the Lord will give you a trembling heart, failing eyes, and a despairing soul.
Your life will hang in suspense before you. You will be afraid day and night and have no assurance of your life.
In the morning you will say, “When will evening come?” And in the evening you will say, “When will morning come?” This will be because of the fear you feel in your heart and the sights your eyes see.

The Lord will take you back to Egypt in ships, by the route of which he told you, “You will never see it again.” There you will be put up for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but there will be no buyer.
These are the words of the covenant that the Lord commanded Moses to establish with the Israelites in the land of Moab, besides the covenant he established with them at Horeb.
Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, “You have seen everything the Lord did before your eyes in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his servants, to all his people, and to all his land.
the great trials your eyes saw, and these signs and wonders that you witnessed.
But to this day the Lord has not given you a heart to understand, eyes to see, or ears to hear.
I led you through the wilderness for forty years. Your clothes did not wear out on you, and your sandals did not wear out on your feet.
You ate no bread and drank no wine or strong drink, so that you might know that I am the Lord your God.
I brought you to this place. Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us in battle, and we defeated them.
We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh.
Keep the commandments of this law and carry them out, so that you may succeed in everything you do.
Today you are standing before the Lord your God, all of you: your tribal leaders, your elders, your scribes, and all the men of Israel,
your families, your wives, and the foreign resident within your camp, from the one who gathers your wood to the one who draws your water.
So that you do not violate the covenant of the Lord your God or the oaths of the Lord your God that he established with you today.
So that he may establish you today as his people, and he may be your God, as he told you and as he swore to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
It is not with you alone that I establish this covenant or this oath,
But with everyone who is here, standing with us today before the Lord our God, and with everyone who is not here with us today.
For you know that we lived in the land of Egypt and passed among the nations through which you passed.
You saw their abominations and their idols of wood and stone, overlaid with silver and gold.

Lest there be among you a man or woman, a family or tribe, whose heart turns away today from the Lord our God to go and serve the gods of those nations; lest there be among you a root that produces gall and wormwood.
And when he hears the words of this oath, he thinks to himself and says, “I will have peace, though I follow my own heart’s desire,” adding drunkenness to thirst.

The Lord will not be willing to forgive him. Instead, the Lord’s anger and jealousy will then grow fierce against that man. Every curse written in this book will come upon him, and the Lord will erase his name from under heaven.
The Lord will single him out for disaster from all the tribes of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this book of the law.

The next generation—your children who arise after you—and foreigners who come from a distant land will speak when they see the afflictions of that land and the diseases that the Lord has brought upon it.

The whole land will be sulfur, salt, and burning. It will not be sown or produce anything, and no vegetation will grow in it. Instead, it will be like Sodom and Gomorrah, like Admah and Zeboiim, which the Lord overthrew in his anger and fury.
All the nations will say, “Why has the Lord done this to this land? Why has this great anger of his blazed up?”
They will say, “Because they abandoned the covenant of the Lord, the God of their ancestors, which he established with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.
They went and served other gods and worshiped them—gods they had not known and that had not been allotted to them.
The Lord’s anger blazed against that land, bringing upon it all the curses written in this book.
The Lord will uproot them from their land in anger, fury, and great wrath, and throw them into another land, as it is today.”
Hidden things belong to the Lord our God, but revealed things belong to us and our children forever, so that we may keep and carry out all the words of this law.
When all these things come upon you—the blessings and curses that I have set before you—and you take them to heart among all the nations where the Lord your God will scatter you,
and you return to the Lord your God and obey his voice according to everything I command you today, you and your children, with all your heart and all your soul,
then the Lord your God will restore you from captivity and have compassion on you. He will again gather you from all the nations among which the Lord your God scattered you.
Even if your scattered people, Israel, are far away at the ends of heaven, from there the Lord your God will gather you, and from there he will bring you near.
The Lord your God will bring you into the land that your ancestors possessed, and you will possess it. He will make you prosper and make you far more numerous than your ancestors.
The Lord your God will circumcise your heart and the hearts of your descendants forever, and you will love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul, so that he may give you life.
The Lord your God will place all these curses upon your enemies and upon those who hate you and have persecuted you.
You will return and obey the voice of the Lord your God, and carry out all his commandments that I command you today.

The Lord your God will make you prosper in all the work of your hands, in the children you bear, in the offspring of your livestock, and in the produce of your land, for your good. For the Lord will again rejoice over you for your good, just as he rejoiced over your ancestors.
When you obey the voice of the Lord your God and keep his commandments and laws written in this book, and return to the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul.
For this commandment that I give you today is not hidden from you, nor is it far away.
It is not in heaven, so that you should say, “Who will go up to heaven for us and bring it to us, so that we may hear it and obey it?”
Nor is it beyond the sea, so that you should say, “Who will cross to the other side of the sea for us and bring it to us, so that we may hear it and obey it?”
Rather, the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, for you to carry it out.
See, today I have set before you life and death, good things and evil things.

I command you today to love the Lord your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments, his laws, and his judgments, so that you may live and increase greatly, and the Lord your God may bless you in the land you are entering to possess.
But if your heart turns aside and you do not listen, and you go astray and bow down to other gods and serve them,
I declare to you today that you will certainly perish. You will not live long in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess.
I call heaven and earth to witness against you today: I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Choose life for yourself, so that you and your descendants may live.

Love the Lord your God, obey his voice, and hold fast to him, for he is your life and the length of your days, so that you may dwell in the land that the Lord swore to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, to give you.
And Moses went and spoke all these words to all Israel.
He said to them, “I am a hundred and twenty years old today. I can no longer go out and come in, and the Lord has told me, ‘You will not cross this Jordan.’”
The Lord your God himself will cross ahead of you. He will destroy these nations before you, and you will dispossess them. Joshua will cross ahead of you, as the Lord has said.
The Lord will do to them as he did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when he destroyed them.
And the Lord will hand them over to you, and you must do to them according to everything I have commanded you.
Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or tremble before them, for the Lord your God goes with you. He will not abandon you or forsake you.

Moses called Joshua and said to him before all Israel, “Be strong and courageous, for you will bring this people into the land that the Lord swore to their ancestors to give them, and you will give it to them as their inheritance.”
The Lord himself goes ahead of you, and he will be with you. He will not abandon you or forsake you. Do not be afraid, do not tremble, and do not be alarmed.
Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the descendants of Levi, who carried the ark of the Lord’s covenant, and to all the elders of the Israelites.
Moses commanded them, saying, “At the end of seven years, at the appointed time in the year of release, at the Festival of Shelters,
when all Israel comes to appear before the Lord your God at the place he chooses, read this law before all Israel so that they can hear it.
Gather the people—men, women, households, and the foreign residents in your towns—so that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord their God, and carefully carry out all the words of this law.
Their children, who have not known it, will hear and learn to fear the Lord their God all the days that you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Look, the time of your death is near. Call Joshua and stand in the tent of meeting, so that I may commission him.” Moses and Joshua went and stood in the tent of meeting.
The Lord appeared in the tent of meeting in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood at the entrance of the tent.

The Lord said to Moses, “You are about to lie down with your ancestors. This people will rise up and go astray after the foreign gods of the land they are entering, among whose inhabitants they will live. They will abandon me and break my covenant that I made with them.

My anger will burn against them on that day. I will abandon them and turn my face away from them. They will be devoured, and many disasters and troubles will come upon them. On that day they will say, ‘These disasters have all happened to me because my God is not among us.’
I will certainly turn my face away from them on that day because of all the evil they have done, because they have turned aside after other gods.
Now write down this song for them and teach it to the Israelites. Put it in their mouths, so that this song may be a witness for me against the Israelites.

For I will bring them into the land that I swore to their ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey. They will eat their fill and live in luxury, and they will turn aside after other gods and serve them. They will provoke me to anger and break my covenant.

When many disasters and troubles come upon them, this song will speak before them as a witness, for it will not be forgotten from the mouths of their descendants. For I know their inclinations and everything they are doing here today, even before I bring them into the land that I swore to their ancestors.”
Moses wrote this song that day and taught it to the Israelites.
He commanded Joshua son of Nun and said to him, “Be strong and courageous, because you will bring the Israelites into the land I swore to give them, and I will be with you.”
When Moses had finished writing all the words of this law in a book,
Moses commanded the Levites who carried the ark of the Lord’s covenant, saying to them,
Take this book of the law and place it beside the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God. It will be there as a witness for you.
For I know your rebelliousness and your stubbornness. Look, even while I am still alive with you today, you have rebelled against the Lord—and you will do so after I die as well.
Gather before me, all you heads of your tribes and your scribes, so that I may speak these words to you and call heaven and earth to witness against you.

For I know that after my death you will become utterly corrupt and turn away from the path I commanded you to follow. Disaster will befall you in the days to come, when you do evil before the Lord and provoke him to anger with the work of your hands.
Moses spoke all the words of this song before the whole assembly of Israel, to the very end.
Listen, heavens, and I will speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
May my teaching fall like rain, and my words descend like dew, like winds over tender grass and like showers over vegetation.
For I will call upon the name of the Lord. Ascribe greatness to our mighty God,
For his works are without flaw, and all his ways are just. He is a faithful God, without injustice, righteous and upright.
They have acted corruptly and are not his—blemished children, a crooked and twisted generation.
Is this how you repay the Lord, foolish and unwise people? Is he not your father, who acquired you? He made you and established you.
Remember the days of old; consider the years of generation after generation. Ask your father, and he will show you; ask your elders, and they will tell you.
When the Most High divided the nations and separated humanity, he established the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the Israelites.
For the Lord’s portion is his people, and Jacob is his allotted inheritance.
He found him in a wilderness land, in a desolate wasteland. He surrounded him, cherished him, and guarded him like the pupil of his eye.
Like an eagle flying over its nest and hovering over its young, he spreads his wings, receives them, and carries them on his mighty wings.
The Lord alone led him, and no foreign god was with him.
He settled him on the heights of the land and fed him the produce of the fields. He made him suck honey from rock and oil from flint.

Butter from cattle and milk from sheep, with the fat of fattened animals, rams, offspring of [?], and young goats, together with the rich fat of wheat; and he gave him wine to drink, the blood of grapes.
Israel grew fat and kicked. He grew fat and strong and acquired possessions. He forgot the God who made him and reviled the Mighty One who saved him.
He made him jealous with foreign gods and angered him with idols.
They sacrificed to demons that were not gods, to gods they had not known. These were new ones, only recently made, whom your ancestors had not feared.
You forgot the Mighty One who fathered you and neglected the God who glorified you.
The Lord saw and became angry, because his sons and daughters had angered him.
He said, “I will turn my face away from them and see what their end will be, for they are a perverse generation, children with no faithfulness in them.”
They made me jealous with what is not God and angered me with their objects of worship. I too will make them jealous with those who are not my people, and I will anger them with a foolish nation.
For a fire is kindled in my anger and burns down to the lowest depths of Sheol. It will consume the earth and its produce and set the foundations of the mountains ablaze.
I will heap disasters upon them and spend my arrows against them.

They will be ravaged by hunger, and evil spirits will be unleashed upon them. I will hand them over to birds and send fanged beasts against them, along with the venom of snakes that crawl in the dust.
Outside, the sword will bereave them, and inside their rooms, terror—young men and young women alike, children together with old men.
I said, ‘Where are they? I will erase their memory from humankind,’
If it were not for the enemy’s fierce anger, lest their enemies exalt themselves and say, “Our own hand has prevailed; it was not the Lord who did all this.”
For they are a people whose judgment is lost, and there is no understanding in them.
If only they were wise and understood this, and considered their end!
One would pursue a thousand, and two would put ten thousand to flight. But their Mighty One handed them over, and the Lord confined them.
For their strength was not like our strength, and our enemies are judges.
For their vine comes from the vine of Sodom and from the planting of Gomorrah. Their grapes are bitter grapes, and their clusters are bitter to them.
Their venom is the venom of a dragon, and the deadly poison of an asp.
Look, it is stored away with me, sealed in the treasuries.
Vengeance is mine; I will repay them when their foot slips. For the day of their ruin is near, and what awaits them is coming swiftly.
For the Lord judges his people and takes comfort in his servants, because he sees that a powerful hand has prevailed, and there is no one to help or support them.
He will say, “Where are their mighty gods, the ones they trusted in,
They used to eat the fat of their sacrifices and drink the wine of their drink offerings. Let them rise now and help you, and let them be your protectors.
See now that I, I am he, and there is no God besides me. I put to death and I bring to life. I wound and I heal, and no one can escape from my hands.
For I have raised my hand toward heaven and said, ‘I live forever.’
I will sharpen the edge of my sword like lightning, and my hand will take hold of judgment. I will repay those who hate me and pay back my enemies.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour flesh: the blood of the slain and the captives, and the crowned head of the enemy.
Now, nations, praise his people, because he avenges the blood of his servants, repays those who hate him, and makes atonement for his land and his people.
Moses came and spoke all the words of this song before the people, he and Joshua son of Nun.
When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
He said to them, “Take to heart all these words that I testify to you today, so that you may command your children to observe and carry out all the words of this law.”
For this is no empty word for you; it is your life. Through this word you will live many days in the land that you are crossing the Jordan to possess.
The Lord spoke to Moses that very day and said to him,
Go up this mountain of Abarim, Mount Nebo, in the land of Moab opposite Jericho, and look at the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites as an inheritance.
Die on the mountain you are climbing, and be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people.
This is because you acted unfaithfully toward me among the Israelites at the waters of strife at Rekem, in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not uphold my holiness among the Israelites.
You may see from a distance the land that I am giving the Israelites, but you will not enter it.”
This is the blessing with which Moses, the servant of God, blessed the Israelites before he died.
And he said, “The Lord came from Sinai and dawned upon us from Seir. He revealed himself from Mount Paran, and with him were some of the myriads of holy ones at his right hand.”
He gave to them, and he also loved the peoples and blessed all his holy ones. They follow at your feet and receive from your word.
Moses handed down the law to us and gave it as an inheritance to the assembly of Jacob.
He will be king in Israel when the leaders of the people and the tribes of Israel gather together.
Let Reuben live and not die, and let him be counted.”
And this he said to Judah: “Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him to his people. Let his hands contend for him, and be his helper against his oppressors.”
And of Levi he said, “Your Thummim and your Urim belong to the faithful man whom you tested with trials and examined at the waters of strife.”
He said of his father and mother, “I have not seen him.” He did not acknowledge his brothers or recognize his children, because they kept your word and guarded your covenant.
They will teach your judgments to Jacob and your laws to Israel. They will place incense before you in your anger, and a whole burnt offering on your altar.
Lord, bless his strength, and be pleased with the work of his hands. Break the backs of those who hate him, and let his enemies never rise.
And of Benjamin he said, “The Lord’s beloved will dwell in peace. He will hover over him all day long and dwell between his shoulders.”
And of Joseph he said, “His land is blessed by the Lord with fruit, with the dew of heaven above and with the deep that lies below.”
with the fruit of the crops produced by the sun and the fruit brought forth by the moon,
with produce from the tops of the eastern mountains and fruit from the everlasting hills,
May the fruit of the earth and all that fills it, and the favor of the one who dwelt in the bush, come upon Joseph’s head, upon the head of the crowned one among his brothers.

His majesty is that of firstborn bulls, and his horns are the horns of a wild ox. With them he will gore the peoples together, as far as the ends of the earth. These are the myriads of Ephraim, and these are the thousands of Manasseh.
Of Zebulun he said: “Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents.
They will call peoples to the mountain, and there they will offer righteous sacrifices, because they will suck the abundance of the seas and the ships hidden in the sand.
Of Gad he said: “Blessed is the one who gives Gad room. He dwells like a lion and breaks the arm together with the head.
He saw the first portion for himself, because there the lawgiver’s portion was reserved. He went out at the head of the people; he carried out the Lord’s righteousness and his judgments with Israel.
Of Dan he said: “Dan is a lion cub suckled in Bashan.”
And of Naphtali he said, “Naphtali is satisfied with favor and full of the Lord’s blessing. He will inherit the west and the south.”
And of Asher he said: “Asher is blessed among sons. May he be favored by his brothers, and may he dip his foot in oil.”
Your shoes will be iron and bronze, and your strength will last as long as your days.”
There is none like the God of Israel, whose chariot is in heaven, who rides to your aid and in his majesty through the highest heavens.
The dwelling of our God is from ancient times, and beneath is the everlasting arm. He will destroy before you the enemy who said, “I will destroy.”
Israel will dwell alone in peace, Jacob’s spring in a land of grain, wine, and oil. The heavens too will sprinkle down dew.

Blessed are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people whose salvation is in the Lord, who gives help? God is your help, and your glory is not in the sword. Your enemies will lie to you, and you will trample on their necks.
Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the summit of the height opposite Jericho. The Lord showed him the whole land of Gilead as far as Dan,
and all Naphtali, and the whole land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and the whole land of Judah as far as the western sea.
the south, and the plain in the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, as far as Zoar.

The Lord said to him, “This is the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’ I have shown it to you with your own eyes, but you will not cross over there.”
And Moses, the servant of the Lord, died there in the land of Moab, at the command of the Lord.
He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor. No one knows his grave to this day.
Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died. His eye had not grown dim, and his cheeks had not shriveled.
The Israelites wept for Moses in the plains of Moab for thirty days. Then the days of weeping in mourning for Moses came to an end.
Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands on him. The Israelites obeyed him and did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Never again did a prophet arise in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face,
